Mr. Bibhuti Ranjan Mohanty, Advocate
 -Versus-
 State of Orissa & another .........
Opposite Parties

Mr. P.K. Maharaj,
 Additional Standing Counsel
 (For O.P. No.1)
 Mr. Malaya Kumar Swain, Advocate

(For O.P. No.2)
 Coram:
 Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra
 Order

At the instance of the opposite party no.2, the F.I.R. in Manamunda P.S. Case No.187 of 2018 arising out of C.T. Case No.341 of 2018 came to be registered against the petitioner for the offences under Sections- 450/376(1)/506 IPC pending in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Kantamal.
2. The parties have now settled their dispute amicably out of the Court.
The opposite party no.2 has married to one Tarini Barik of Telbahali and blessed with two children.
Due to these changing circumstances, the opposite party no.2 is not willing to further proceed with this matter and seeks to drop the proceeding against the petitioner.

3. The petitioner and the opposite party no.2 have filed separate affidavits dated 15.02.2024, inter alia, stating that they have settled their dispute at the intervention of the well-wishers and village gentries.
The husband of the opposite party no.2 is also present in Court today.
4. The petitioner and the opposite party no.2 are present in person in Court today.
They are represented by their respective counsels.
They have also filed their respective self-attested Aadhaar Cards to establish their identity, which are taken on record.

5. Mr. Maharaj, learned Additional Standing Counsel submits that since the parties have now settled their dispute out of the Court and the opposite party no.2 has already married and blessed with two children, continuance of the prosecution against the petitioner would be in futility.

Therefore, there is no impediment in quashing the F.I.R.
